title: Enterprise Top 10: West Brook Bruins rising up the local rankings - NewsBreak
text:
By Matt Faye ,
1 days ago West Brook had no trouble with Silsbee on Friday night in a battle of unbeaten teams at Doggett Family Stadium in Beaumont. (Photo by Jarrod Brown) One game can shift the hierarchy of local high school football. This past week, West Brook's big win led to some significant changes in the Enterprise Top 10 power rankings.
In a game that highlighted the local schedule last weekend, West Brook dominated Silsbee for a 49-14 victory that kept the Bruins unbeaten. Now, the Bruins have catapulted all the way up to the No. 3 spot in the power rankings.
Meanwhile, Silsbee is still ranked but falls a few spots. The Tigers will have plenty of chances to get back on track and prove their worth among the region's top teams.
RELATED: West Brook stays unbeaten with decisive win over Silsbee
The Enterprise’s weekly top 10 isn’t based on who would win head-to-head. In the UIL classification system with varying school sizes, it wouldn’t make sense to judge Southeast Texas teams that way.
Instead, we build the local top 10 with a power ranking approach. A team’s ranking is based on its performance relative to their classification, not a hypothetical head-to-head game.
Enough explaining. Here are the Enterprise Top 10 power rankings entering Week 5 of the season.
1. Port Neches-Groves (3-0)
Coming off a bye week, Port Neches-Groves is eager to show why it's the top-ranked team on this list. The District 8-5A-II schedule starts with a huge road game at Lake Creek.
2. Port Arthur Memorial (4-0)
The Titans' offense can't be stopped right now. They come off a 52-14 win over Cleburne last week, marking the latest blowout victory for Memorial this season. District 9-5A-I action starts this week with a short road trip to Beaumont United.
3. West Brook (4-0)
This is the best West Brook has looked in a long time. The Bruins put a beatdown on Silsbee last week, and quarterback Tam Anderson is showing why he's one of the region's best signal callers. It's been a great start, and the Bruins get a break this week during their bye.
4. Bridge City (3-0)
Maybe the most under-the-radar team in Southeast Texas is Bridge City. The Cardinals are still unbeaten, but how long will it last? Like many other local teams, Bridge City starts district play this week with a home game against Lumberton in 10-4A-I.
5. Newton (3-1)
The Eagles have won three straight games and now get ready for the District 12-3A-II opener at Anderson-Shiro. Newton's season-opening loss to West Orange-Stark feels like forever ago. The Eagles are rolling after a 36-16 victory over DeRidder this past week.
6. Silsbee (3-1)
The sky is certainly not falling in Silsbee. Yes, the Tigers lost to a much bigger West Brook team, but there's no reason to panic. Silsbee still has a great chance at a district title. The Tigers will play one final tune-up against Hitchcock before their league schedule begins.
7. Hamshire-Fannett (3-1)
The Longhorns won their first three games of the season, but came back down to Earth last weekend. Hamshire-Fannett suffered a tough loss to Almeta Crawford, 63-21. The Longhorns' offense is incredible. Now, the defense needs to fix a few things before a home game against Stafford.
8. Orangefield (3-1)
The Bobcats had a nice bounce-back win last week over St. Louis Catholic out of Louisiana. It came after Orangefield's close loss to Bridge City in the Bayou Bowl two weeks ago. Up next is a good matchup against Hardin to begin the District 10-3A-I schedule.
9. Woodville (3-1)
Make it three straight wins for Woodville since the season-opening loss to Orangefield. Most recently, the Eagles had no trouble taking down Diboll during a 46-7 road victory. This week, district play begins with a home game against Trinity.
10. West Orange-Stark (2-2)
The Mustangs are the only two-loss team in the rankings. They got back on track with a 52-23 win over Bellaire Episcopal this past week. West Orange-Stark now looks ahead to a tough challenge from Almeta Crawford, a team that just dismantled Hamshire-Fannett.
